description: Changing the pilot country from Serbia to North Macedonia before G0 required edits to about thirty files because country, chapter, dates, languages and examples were written into the codebooks, procedures and rules.
scaling_implication: Every new country or chapter would have needed the same sweep. Keeping run-specific settings in the run record, CLAUDE.md and the limits log makes the method reusable.
recommendation: Keep method documents country-neutral; add a check before each new run that searches the method documents for country, chapter and date terms.

description: A scope combining one chapter with a cross-cutting theme (technology and AI) could not be expressed with chapter and cluster fields alone, so theme tags planned for a later stage had to be brought forward.
scaling_implication: Scaling across chapters and clusters will need more cross-cutting themes; the materiality test and scope basis need testing at G3 to G5 before more themes are added.
recommendation: Review how well the materiality test and the out_of_scope check work at G3 and G5 before defining further themes.

description: The helper tools depend on system software (text recognition with Macedonian and Albanian language data, PDF rendering) that was not installed in the working environment and was not recorded anywhere before stage 0.
scaling_implication: Each new country or language needs its own text recognition data and a test with a sample in that script before extraction starts.
recommendation: Keep tools/requirements.txt current; add a scanned sample in each new language to tools/tests/test_tools.py before a new country is added.

description: The rule that the freeze date falls just after the annual enlargement package did not match the date set at G0: the 2026 package had not appeared by the freeze date, so the newest annual report in the run is from 2025.
scaling_implication: Every country shares the same package date, so a freeze date set before the package leaves all countries a year behind; a date set after it must wait for publication.
recommendation: At G0, check whether the year's package has been published before fixing the freeze date, and record which annual report is the latest in scope.

description: A cross-cutting theme makes the whole of each annual report and the screening reports for all clusters relevant, so the EU source base is much larger than for a single chapter.
scaling_implication: Workload grows with the number of themes rather than the number of chapters; adding themes will need more extraction effort and a sharper materiality test.
recommendation: Measure extraction time and the share of theme items found incidental at G3 before adding further themes.

description: Major publishers (OECD and SIGMA, UNDP, Council of Europe, some Council and national pages) block automated downloads, so several core sources need manual retrieval by the analyst.
scaling_implication: Manual retrieval grows with every country added and could become the bottleneck of acquisition.
recommendation: Plan a manual retrieval step in the procedure, or seek permitted access routes (publisher APIs or bulk downloads) before scaling.

description: Almost all national government sources in scope are only in Macedonian (some also in Albanian), so most evidence on the country response will rest on machine translation capped at Medium confidence.
scaling_implication: Every new country brings its own language; without a reviewer who reads it, country-response evidence stays capped at Medium.
recommendation: Before scaling, decide whether to recruit reviewers who read the national languages, and measure at G3 how often machine translation affects extraction.

description: Acquisition relied on an unversioned working script; three recording errors were caught and corrected, which shows the step needs a tested tool.
scaling_implication: At larger scale, recording errors in the register would be harder to spot by hand.
recommendation: Turn the acquisition script into a tested project tool (download, fingerprint, file, convert, register) before the next run.

description: Searching for sources with parallel agents, one per group of families, and checking every URL before download found 99 documents in under an hour.
scaling_implication: The approach can scale to more countries and chapters, provided agent-supplied metadata is checked before registration.
recommendation: Keep the per-family split; add a metadata check against the first page of each document.

description: In the sample, the technology theme produced about two and a half times as many items as Chapter 2 (742 against 288), many of them sector IT systems of doubtful relevance, at about 6 to 7 hours of agent time for 11 sources.
scaling_implication: A cross-cutting theme read across whole reports multiplies extraction volume; adding themes or countries would multiply it again.
recommendation: Tighten the materiality test before full extraction (rule issue R1) and measure the effect on the next sample.

description: The quote check cannot verify quotes that cross a page break because printed page numbers and running headers sit between the pages, so sound items were shortened or dropped.
scaling_implication: Longer documents and other publishers' layouts will make this more frequent.
recommendation: Teach the quote check to skip page-number and header lines at page boundaries (rule issue R4).

description: Parallel extraction agents applied the same rules in different ways where the rules were silent (repeated text, sub-area progress wording, chapter basis), which makes counts and later judgements inconsistent.
scaling_implication: The more sources and agents, the more such differences will accumulate unless the rules cover these cases.
recommendation: Add the clarifications in rule issues R3, R7, R10 and R11 and give every extraction agent the same worked examples.

description: The automatic quote check confirms that a quote appears at its location but not that it is cut to the claim; three quotes that began too early passed it unnoticed until an agent re-read them.
scaling_implication: At larger volumes, mis-cut quotes will only be caught by sampling, so they could reach judgements.
recommendation: Warn on quotes longer than three sentences and keep quote boundaries in the reviewer checklist (rule issue R18).

description: Applying analyst decisions R1 to R11 by revising the sample, rather than re-extracting it, took about half an hour per source and cut the sample from 1,054 to 732 items with every quote still verified; it also surfaced the next layer of boundary questions.
scaling_implication: Rule refinement in short loops on a fixed sample is cheap, and each loop exposes boundary cases that need a written rule before scaling.
recommendation: Keep the revise-and-compare loop at G3 for every new chapter or theme, with a fixed sample and a comparison sheet.

description: The manual extraction check was reduced to simplified hand-coding of three passages and a stratified sample of 70 items, focused on missed and misclassified items, instead of reviewing every extracted item.
scaling_implication: Reviewing every item does not scale; a fixed-size stratified sample keeps the analyst workload roughly constant as volume grows.
recommendation: Confirm at G3 whether the sample gave enough confidence; if so, make the stratified sample the standard G3 check in procedure P2.

description: Independent agents (a blind coder and reviewers who took no part in extraction) checked all 725 sample items in under 15 minutes elapsed, recorded verdicts before fixing, and gave usable error rates without analyst time.
scaling_implication: Independent agent review scales with volume where human row review cannot; the remaining gap is that no human has checked extraction directly.
recommendation: Keep agent QA as the standard G3 check; add a small human spot check (about 10 items) when a new country or language is added.

description: The main extraction weaknesses are missed neighbouring claims (about 14% of in-scope claims, mostly low or medium importance) and quotes that hold two claims; types and references are almost always right.
scaling_implication: At full scale, misses concentrate in sections far from the chapter headings; a second screening pass is cheaper than a human check.
recommendation: In full extraction, add a second-pass check per source: keyword screen for the theme and a split check for two-claim quotes, run by a different agent.

description: The EU accession material says almost nothing specific about artificial intelligence (two EU requirement items in six years of reports); AI evidence for the country comes mainly from a national audit, so an AI focus cannot rest on EU requirements alone.
scaling_implication: For emerging topics, EU reports lag behind policy; scaling a theme like AI will depend more on national and international sources than the method assumes.
recommendation: Treat thin EU coverage as a finding in itself, and widen the national and IO source requirements for emerging topics before scaling.

description: Drafting the taxonomy in two parallel parts (Chapter 2 and technology) produced an overlapping issue on electronic exchange of social security data, because each drafter treated the shared items as its own.
scaling_implication: With more chapters and themes, overlaps between parallel drafts will multiply.
recommendation: Add a merge step after parallel drafting: list items mapped to issues in both parts and resolve each overlap before the gate.
